text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Managers of Montazhspetsbank commercial bank and a team of investigators looking into alleged irregularities in the bank's management exchange accusations of impropriety.
- The World Bank is to decide today whether to grant an $800 million credit to Russia.
- Russian natural gas monopolist Gazprom could see its board of directors shaken up at the forthcoming shareholders' meeting.
- The city of St Petersburg has partially used the money received from a eurobond issue to pay back its debts to commercial banks.
- A new type of security -- corporate bonds -- could appear in Russia as early as September.
- Yuri Bespalov, new president of major oil producer Rosneft, is tightening its grip on the company.
- The Central Bank and the Federal Securities Commission say they are working to heal the rift between the two institutions regarding the rules for the securities market in Russia.
SEVODNYA
- Cargo vessel Progress rammed the Mir space station.
- There is no doubt the World Bank will grant an $800 million credit to Russia.
- Russian timber industry faces privatisation and a fierce struggle for control over its main producers.
- The government does not conceal it is annoyed by the Duma's decision to go on holiday without passing a string of major laws.
- Twenty percent of shares in Slavneft oil producer may be sold off before this winter.
- The authorities are planning comprehensive checks of all strong alcohol distributors to make sure they comply with new tougher sales rules to be introduced from July 1.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin goes to China to strengthen Russia's ties with its eastern neighbour.
- The Islamic Taleban movement in Afghanistan is not planning an ideological expansion into CIS countries.
- Investigators are probing an alleged corruption case involving top managers of the giant Krasnoyarsk metals company.
- Russia should temporarily lease its irreplacable natural resources to foreign companies rather than sell them.
- Russian telecommunications industry is booming and the fight for a bigger stake in the expanding market is likely to intensify.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The government will implement its financial strategy regardless of the Duma's unwillingness to approve it.
- The new tax code, if finally approved by the Duma, will significantly cut income tax.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Russia's Gazprom is about to pay what it owes to the budget, a move which will make it possible for the government to honour its debts to pensioners.
- The government is likely to accumulate new debts to pensioners in the wake of the Duma's decision to increase pensions.
-- Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
